title: Can a wrong guess help you learn? Meet pretesting

sources.name: Richland, Kornell & Kao (2009) — The pretesting effect: five experiments and their limits

practice: Try Sequence and see whether you can explain the pattern behind your answer.

sections.html:
Trying a question before studying the correct information can sometimes help you remember it later. Researchers call this pretesting. The studying afterwards matters: guessing alone does not teach the answer.

Try a small example: what comes next in 3, 6, 12, 24? Keep your answer and your reason in mind.
sections.title: Why try before studying?

sections.html:
In a 2009 study by Richland, Kornell and Kao, five experiments used a passage about vision. Some participants tried questions before reading; others had more time to study.

The pretested material was remembered better later, even when the analysis included only questions answered incorrectly at first.

That does not mean every wrong guess helps. Participants studied the correct information afterwards, and benefits for material they had not been pretested on were inconsistent.
sections.title: A wrong first answer was not the end

sections.html:
With the rule “double the previous number”, the next number is 48: 24 × 2 = 48.

A short sequence can fit more than one rule. Compare your explanation with doubling: where, if anywhere, did your idea take another turn?

This example shows how to compare an attempt with an explanation. It does not measure a memory benefit.
sections.title: The explanation is the useful part

sections.html:
Before a short article, turn its title into a question. Jot down an answer, then read and check it.

  • Keep the attempt brief.
  • Find the correct explanation.
  • Put the corrected answer in your own words.

No need to invent a mistake. If you already know the answer, check your reasoning.

Later, close the page and try recalling it. That is a separate step, covered in our guide to remembering quiz answers.
sections.title: Give yourself one question to look out for

description: Pretesting means trying a question before you study. See what a study found about wrong first answers, then try a small example.
